description: The fingerprints that pin the build of an internet-facing VPN or edge appliance from outside (cveFeed.version_catalogue, the edge entries): a build string or a header a static asset carries, and the published table that maps it to a release. Every table names its source, the commit or document it was read from, and its licence; every entry cites the line it was read from. An entry whose fingerprint maps to one release gives an exact reading; one that maps to several (a date several releases share, a build line) gives a range, which is an inference and is never matched as a version inside an affected range. Add an entry only from a public source whose licence allows it, and say which. Products left out (no public fingerprint with a compatible licence, or no reliable one): Cisco ASA and FTD, SonicWall SMA and SSL-VPN, F5 BIG-IP, Check Point, MOVEit Transfer, Sophos XG (docs/PIPELINE.md, Edge appliance builds).

netscaler.note: One firmware serves both products: a build is read as both, and each CVE is matched against the product its record names (NVD: citrix:netscaler_application_delivery_controller, citrix:netscaler_gateway; the CNA's records: NetScaler ADC, NetScaler Gateway).

pan-os.note: NVD: paloaltonetworks:pan-os; the CNA's records: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS.

fortios.note: NVD and the CNA: fortinet:fortios / Fortinet FortiOS.

connect-secure.note: NVD: ivanti:connect_secure, pulsesecure:pulse_connect_secure; the CNA's records: Ivanti Connect Secure, and Pulse Connect Secure with no vendor.

netscaler_rdx_stamp.what: The gzip header timestamp (MTIME, bytes 4 to 8, little-endian) of /vpn/js/rdx/core/lang/rdx_en.json.gz: the build time of the NetScaler firmware that serves it. One timestamp, one build.
netscaler_rdx_stamp.notice: Derived from Fox-IT's citrix-netscaler-triage (Apache License 2.0). Changes: the CSV in the script was converted to JSON, and its rows whose version is 'unknown' were left out.

netscaler_vhash.what: The ?v= value the /vpn/index.html login page appends to its own resources (rdx.css?v=<32 hex>): a value per build. Not every build sends one.
netscaler_vhash.notice: Derived from Fox-IT's citrix-netscaler-triage (Apache License 2.0). Changes: the vhash column of the script's CSV, converted to JSON; rows with no vhash or an 'unknown' version left out.

panos_release_dates.what: The release date of each PAN-OS version. The GlobalProtect portal's static files carry their build time in Last-Modified and in the last 8 hex digits of their ETag; a build time within two days of a release date makes that release a candidate. A date can match several releases (of several branches), and the table ends in April 2024: a reading is always a range (inferred), and a build time after the table's last date reads nothing.

fortios_etag.what: FortiOS before 7.2.6, 7.4.0 to 7.4.1, and every 7.0 and 6.4 release, answer the SSL-VPN front page with an ETag whose last 8 hex digits are the build time (CVE-2024-23662, FG-IR-23-224: 'may allow an unauthenticated attacker to fingerprint the device version via HTTP requests'). Such an ETag on a FortiGate's front page puts its release in those ranges: a range (inferred), never a release. The build time is shown as evidence; no public table with a compatible licence maps it to a release.
fortios_etag.licence: Vendor advisory (facts, cited); the nuclei template that reads the ETag this way is MIT (ProjectDiscovery). No data is copied from either.

entries.cite: https://www.fortiguard.com/psirt/FG-IR-23-224 (affected: 7.4.0 through 7.4.1, 7.2.0 through 7.2.5, 7.0 all versions, 6.4 all versions)

connect_secure_lines.what: Pulse Connect Secure states its version in two static files a browser fetches without signing in: /dana-na/nc/nc_gina_ver.txt (8.x: <PARAM NAME="ProductVersion" VALUE="8.3.7.61383">) and the Host Checker installer /dana-cached/hc/HostCheckerInstaller.osx (9.x: <key>version</key><string>9.1.11.12173</string>). The four numbers are the line, the release and the build: 9.1.11.12173 is 9.1R11 build 12173. The build names one of the release's service releases (9.1R11.4), but no public table with a compatible licence maps builds to service releases, so a reading is the range 9.1R11 to 9.1R11.x (inferred). The 22.x Host Checker version does not name the Connect Secure release in that form and reads nothing.
connect_secure_lines.licence: Paths and formats are facts cited from public research; the nuclei template that reads both files is MIT (ProjectDiscovery). No data is copied.
